build.summary:
I built work package diag-anatomy-variants. Typecheck passes. All the new tests pass, as do the tests of the modules I changed, with one exception: two assertions in src/types/caseModel.test.ts now fail. That file belongs to found-case-model-types, not to this package. It says random cases never contain the new variants, which this package's design changes on purpose (details under outOfScope).

What now works:
- **Analytic anatomy** (src/simulation/anatomy.ts) builds every new variant: the circumflex from the right sinus or from the proximal RCA, the RCA from the left sinus, the left main from the right sinus, high ostia, a large conus with its own ostium, and a very dilated root (radius 28 mm). The sinus azimuths stay the usual ones, so the physics root keeps its proper cusps. Every existing case gives a bit-identical model (fingerprint before and after over the library, PCI scenarios, diagnostic scenarios and 300 generated cases).
- **Render tree** (src/render/xray/coronaryGrowth.ts, coronaryAtlas.ts):
  - A left main from the right sinus runs between the aorta and the pulmonary trunk to its usual bifurcation.
  - A circumflex from the proximal RCA runs behind the aorta, keeping the circumflex calibre scale and segment numbers.
  - A fistula runs from the proximal LAD to the pulmonary trunk.
  - The anomalous circumflex and its branches now fill with a right-sided injection, so a left injection leaves the lateral wall empty.
- **Contrast** (contrastTransport.ts): the fistula is a sink that feeds no blush, and a circumflex with its own right-sinus ostium fills slightly late, from the sinus. I added a function for how much of a sinus injection or aortogram reaches each ostium, with Brilakis's 60 mL over 3 s. Nothing calls it yet (see outOfScope).
- **Physics** (src/physics/coronaryLumens.ts): reports the ostia from the render tree in the classifier's names, and keeps the circumflex from the RCA as a lumen.
- **Case generator** (caseGenerator.ts): random cases carry one anomaly at 1.5%, the midpoint of Oxford's 1–2% (the split between anomalies is a model parameter). The case name never mentions it. Suggested catheters, coaching hints for guided mode, and difficulty ratings now cover the new variants. The usual catheter stays first in the list, because the lab opens each case with it.
- **Scenario pack** (diagnosticScenarios/anatomy.ts and anatomy.launch.ts): eight scenarios, with case names that only describe the presentation. The four anomalous-origin scenarios raise 'anomalous-origin' for the rest of the case at the first injection.

Realism: I re-captured the offscreen baseline as set wp-dav. The scorecard is 189/236, the same as the baseline, with no rows lost or gained. All frames of the six reference views, the fluoroscopy and flush companions, dev_guide and dev_wire are byte-identical to the baseline. dev_balloon and dev_stent differ only because their capture metadata shows other balloon and stent pressures (8 to 6 atm, 10 to 9 atm), which come from another package's change to the PCI equipment catalogue. Those two runs are not in the pass count.

build.notes:
Snapshots of the six pre-existing listed files and the .started marker are in datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/diag-anatomy-variants/. The three other listed files did not exist before. I also added one new test file outside the list, src/ui/sim/modules/anatomy.tips.test.ts, placed beside the event source (the scenario script module) as the acceptance asks.

Design choices worth knowing:
- **Ostium.az** for the left main and RCA stays at the usual sinus azimuth when the artery is anomalous. The real position is in pos and dir, and ostiumAz() gives its azimuth. This stops the physics root (lumen.ts rootGeom, which builds its cusps from lm.az and rca.az) from deforming. The earlier code moved rca.az into the left sinus for an anomalous RCA, which would have squashed the cusps.
- **Optional model fields** (lm in sinusOf, sinusAz, usual, lcxOrigin) are set only for anomalous cases, so every existing model is bit-identical.
- **Starting catheter:** the lab opens a case with recommendedCatheters[0]. For the anomaly variants the usual catheter (JL4 or JR4, TIG from the radial) stays first and the Amplatz shapes come after it, so the case does not open with the answer loaded.
- **Separate ostia** give way to an anomalous left main or circumflex, in both the analytic model and the genome, so random combinations stay consistent.
- **Tips:** diag-interp-anomalous-cx-search needs vessel LCx in the context. In the live lab that happens when the rod physics reports the tip in the circumflex, or in the finish step with an empty lateral wall (finishContexts). With the simple mechanics during the study, the context names LM or RCA, so only diag-anomalous-origin-image-first shows mid-study.
- **Browser:** the rod physics was off in the lab ('simple' mechanics), so the browser check used the analytic engagement. In my browser tab I hid the pre-brief panel to take the screenshots and set the shared UI section back to 'structural-lab' afterwards.
- **Capture files:** the new set is in datasets/tmp/captures/wp-dav/, and its scorecard is at datasets/tmp/realism/reports/wp-dav/scorecard_matched.md and .json.

review.verdict:
Partly done: changes requested before the package can close. I re-checked the builder's claims and they hold. The typecheck is clean. Both of the package's test files pass (25 tests), and src/render/xray/anatomy.test.ts passes (48). compare_sets.py baseline wp-dav gives 189 vs 189, with no rows lost or gained. The diffs against the snapshots are additive and match the report. The only other src/ files changed since .started are the transseptal files, which belong to structural-transseptal-hands-on. The anatomy core (analytic ostia, render-tree courses, fistula sink, fill-list routing, case-generator prior, scenario pack, launch links) is done well. Every clinical number in it traces to the module text (1–2%, 0.2–0.7%, 60 mL over 3 s, 4 Fr through a 6 Fr AL3, the diameter-plus-one rule) or is labelled MODEL PARAMETER. British English is clean, and nothing new allocates per frame.

Four things stop it closing:
1. The live lab shows a wrong picture when the learner seats a catheter in the anomalous circumflex's own right-sinus ostium.
2. On a selective RCA run, the anomalous circumflex fills fully. The module says it fills faintly.
3. Three design items are not built: filling the coronaries from a sinus injection or aortogram, the aortogram action, and the multipurpose-catheter dissection hazard. Without them the scenarios' 'locate' checks cannot be met.
4. src/types/caseModel.test.ts now has two failing tests.

One regression was not reported: the mentor's rotation analysis now aims at the empty sinus in the anomalous-origin cases.

findings.where: src/simulation/engagement.ts:332-341 and src/physics/lumen.ts:903-910 (outside the package; touches the package's anomalous-lcx-right-sinus fill routing in coronaryGrowth.ts anomalyFinish)
findings.problem: In the analytic model, model.leftOstium2 always counts as the 'left' side, and so does ostiaOf's 'left2' in the physics classifier. For anomalous-lcx-right-sinus that ostium sits in the right sinus, 22 degrees round from the RCA. A JR4 seated in it, or passing it while turning towards the RCA, therefore reports selective-lm and gets the LEFT fill list. Since anomalyFinish moved the circumflex system to fillId 'RCA', that injection draws the LM and LAD from a catheter in the right sinus, and not the vessel the catheter is in. This is a wrong image on a live screen in the main scenario, diag-anomalous-cx-retroaortic, whose 'image' check asks the learner to engage this vessel. The builder listed it under outOfScope but still marked the browser criterion met.
findings.fix: Schedule an amendment to engagement.ts (owner diag-engagement-fallback) and to the physics classifier mapping. When leftEval came from model.leftOstium2 and model.sinusOf?.lcx === 'right', classify the side as 'right' (selective-rca or coaxial-rca). For that ostium, give a fill list of the circumflex system only, not RIGHT_VESSELS. One way: keep the anomalous circumflex's fill key separate (for example fillId 'LCx' plus a contrast.ts rule that removes LCx, OM1 and OM2 from the left list and adds them to the right list when model.sinusOf.lcx === 'right'), so that a selective circumflex injection does not also fill the RCA. Add a test: a tip at model.leftOstium2 gives a fill list containing LCx and not LAD.

findings.problem: A circumflex with its own right-sinus ostium is side 'right' with fillId 'RCA', so on a selective RCA injection it gets the full right-side capture and opacifies like the RCA, only 0.6 s later. The module text the package cites (09-interpreting.ts:1199, 'the vessel outlines faintly on the RCA injection') and the code comment both say faint. As built, the RCA run shows the whole lateral wall brightly, which makes the missing circumflex easy to spot and does not teach the search the tip describes.
findings.fix: In contrastTransport.ts (in the file list), add a MODEL PARAMETER inlet share, for example SINUS_FED = { delayS: 0.6, share: 0.3 }. Record it on TransportNet (for example inletShare: Map<string, number> for the parentless right-side LCx and every vessel under it), and multiply the ostial concentration by it wherever transport turns the seat capture into vessel concentration. Keep share 1 for anomalous-lcx-from-rca, which is a true RCA branch. Test that the peak concentration in the LCx is clearly below the RCA's on a selective RCA run for anomalous-lcx-right-sinus, and unchanged for anomalous-lcx-from-rca.

findings.where: Package design: root-plume filling, the pigtail aortogram and the multipurpose-catheter dissection hazard (src/render/xray/sceneBuilder.ts, src/simulation/contrast.ts, src/state/useSimulatorStore.ts, src/physics/legacyBridge.ts / src/ui/physics/physicsDevices.ts)
findings.problem: Three items in the design are not built. (1) 'A sinus injection or a pigtail aortogram (60 mL over 3 s) fills the anomalous vessel from the root plume': rootInjectionShares() and AORTOGRAM exist but nothing calls them, and a non-selective puff still fills no coronary. (2) There is no aortogram action. (3) 'A multipurpose catheter pushed into an anomalous ostium raises the wall-force dissection hazard' is not implemented. The scenarios' 'locate' checks (diag-rca-from-left-sinus, diag-lm-from-right-sinus, diag-high-ostia) and the tip text all depend on (1). The learner is told to find the ostium with a sinus injection, and the lab cannot show it. The ostiaFromTree() and rootInjectionShares() exports are also unused outside tests.
findings.fix: Do not close the package as complete. Record these as a follow-up package that lists sceneBuilder.ts, contrast.ts and useSimulatorStore.ts. A non-selective injection with engagement 'sinus-level' should draw each ostium's tree with rootInjectionShares(ostiaFromRenderTree(tree), tipPos) as its seat capture. Add a pigtail aortogram action that uses AORTOGRAM and the contrast budget. The same follow-up should list legacyBridge.ts and physicsDevices.ts for the MP wall-force hazard at ostia where model.sinusOf differs from the usual (or where model.usual is set). Until then, mark the design criteria 'not met' in the package notes.

findings.where: src/simulation/diagnosticScenarios/anatomy.ts:33 (ANOMALY_SEEN) and its use in diag-anomalous-cx-retroaortic and diag-high-ostia
findings.problem: The trigger is firstInjection: 'any', so 'anomalous-origin', and with it the tip 'Anomalous origin: image the root before choosing', fires on whatever injection comes first. In the circumflex case a first selective RCA injection fills the circumflex fully and leaves no territory empty, yet the event and tip still appear. That gives the anomaly away, against the plan's 'raised when the first left or right injection leaves a territory empty, or after a sinus injection'. In diag-high-ostia a first injection after normal engagement does the same. 'any' is right for the RCA-from-left and LM-from-right cases.
findings.fix: For diag-anomalous-cx-retroaortic use two triggers: { id: 'anomaly-left', when: { firstInjection: 'left' }, do: [raise anomalous-origin, hold 'case'] } and { id: 'anomaly-sinus', when: { firstInjection: 'any', engagement: ['sinus-level'] }, do: [...] }, plus whichever other non-selective EngagementKinds the store reports. For diag-high-ostia use only the sinus-injection trigger. Update anatomy.tips.test.ts to inject on the left side first and add a case where a first RCA injection raises nothing.

findings.problem: AL1 reaches 4/5 only with a procedure written in the test (amplatzTo: 45 corrections, aimed at model.rca.pos). The builder reports that the shared manoeuvres.amplatzLeftTechnique (30 corrections) gives AL1 1/5, and that JR4 turned anticlockwise gives 2/5. The test compares against JR4 clockwise only (1/5). It does not show that the anatomy alone makes Amplatz shapes work where Judkins fail. The builder also notes that the lab ran with 'simple' mechanics, where the catheter shape may not matter at all.

Name the 45-correction aimed procedure in the test title and record its counts, and the 30-correction result, in the package notes. Add a follow-up for the analytic fallback (engagement.ts), so that under 'simple' mechanics the anomalous ostia also depend on catheter shape.
